why: "each time a model in that unit makes a melee attack that targets a unit (excluding MONSTERS and VEHICLES), add 1 to the Hit roll": the note is now only "+1 to hit" (calc {hit:1}), with vs none Monster/Vehicle. Beacons of Rage is tagged "(Aura)", so 22.01 puts the Eightbound within their own aura and selfAlways is right; no table condition is left on this mark.

"If that attack targets a unit that is Below Half-strength, add 1 to the Wound roll as well" (Wahapedia repeats "(excluding MONSTERS and VEHICLES)" there): note "+1 to wound rolls", calc {wound:1}, vs none Monster/Vehicle. Below Half-strength is the target’s state in the battle, a table condition, so having no always/selfAlways (an unticked box, for other units and its own) is right.

where: pubstomper · Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with wings
why: "Each time this model makes an attack that targets a CHARACTER unit, re-roll a Hit roll of 1 and re-roll a Wound roll of 1": vs any Character and the note match, and the only condition is the target’s keyword, so always is right. An attached unit with a CHARACTER leader is a CHARACTER unit (19.03).

where: pubstomper · Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with wings
why: "(if that attack targets a PSYKER CHARACTER unit, you can re-roll the Hit roll and you can re-roll the Wound roll instead)": vs all [Psyker, Character] needs both keywords, as the words do, and dmVs now handles all (the Norn Emissary, PSYKER but not CHARACTER, is ruled out). Target keywords only, so always is right; with both boxes on, the calculator keeps the full re-roll over the 1s, which is the "instead".

"Each time a model in this unit makes a ranged attack, re-roll a Wound roll of 1." The note is now only that unconditional part, calc {rrWound:'1s'} says it exactly, and always is right. It is the Rubric Marines’ (bodyguard) ability, so it covers the Sorcerer’s attacks too (19.04).

"If the attack targets a unit within range of an objective marker you do not control, you can re-roll the Wound roll instead." The when and calc {rrWound:'all'} match; it depends on the table (objective markers), so having no always (an unticked box) is right.

Wahapedia’s Grand Coven rule (pubstomper takes that detachment): "In your Command phase, you can select one of the abilities listed below … You can only select each of these abilities once per battle." A choice, so it is an unticked box with a pick and no always; needs Faction: Thousand Sons ("THOUSAND SONS models from your army"). Each pick says what its ability says, limited to [PSYCHIC] weapons: Imbued Manifestation "Add 6" to the Range characteristic of ranged Psychic weapons" = +6" range (a melee weapon has no range, so it reaches ranged weapons only); Psychic Maelstrom "add 1 to the Wound roll" = +1 to wound rolls; Wrath of the Immaterium "have the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] ability".

"Each time this model makes an attack that targets a MONSTER or VEHICLE unit, add 1 to the Hit roll." vs any Monster/Vehicle and the note "+1 to hit rolls" match, and the only condition is the target’s keywords, so always is right.

"If that target is TITANIC or TOWERING, add 1 to the Wound roll as well." vs any Titanic/Towering, note "+1 to wound rolls", always (target keywords only). The words also need a MONSTER/VEHICLE target, which vs cannot add here, but all 9 TITANIC/TOWERING units in data.js are MONSTER or VEHICLE, so no target gets it wrongly.

"Aegis Protocol: Add 1 to the Toughness characteristic of KASTELAN ROBOT models in that unit." defCalc {t:1, model:'Kastelan Robot'} matches. Without defAlways it is now an unticked box, which fits "you can select one protocol … it remains in that protocol until it enters a different one", a choice the player makes.
